issues.reason: The first half stands — (Ordinal <entity> <n> <scale>) is defined as the entity's rank on an ordering ("Priya was the first to respond" -> (Ordinal priya 1 respond)), so the atom asserts Coraline was the first person ever to attend, which the text does not state; the second half does not — "as a Keeper" is not dropped, it is recorded one line earlier as (Member coraline_ash keeper).

gaps_confirmed: "for the first time" — an ordinal over one agent's own occurrences of an event: Ordinal ranks an entity against others on a scale, Again/Still/Already record a prior same-type event rather than its absence, and Every/TimesPer need a stated period or rate, so "the Nth occurrence of this agent V-ing" has no carrier.

A capitalized calendar period used as a nominal argument ("the lessons of Year 1", "the policies of Year 2"): (Year <n>) is defined only as a Time-role filler, and even if Names and casing licensed a year_1 entity (a capitalized run exceeding the bare class word), nothing links that entity to the (Year 1) time term the same period takes in a Time slot, so the two records of one period could never join.
new_gaps: Day-of-year ordinal in a non-Gregorian calendar ("day 640 of Year 2"): (Day <n>) is the day-of-month granularity — the seeded strict ordering reads it as same-year-month day — so a day counted within a year has no licensed term.

Role-capacity "as a N" adjunct on an event ("attended the Council as a Keeper", "served as chair"): the surface-preposition oblique is defined for PPs naming what the activity is about or directed at, and a bare typing atom on the person states the capacity timelessly instead of as the capacity in which the event was performed.
defect_summary: The instruction set licenses no form for "for the first time" as a first-occurrence-for-this-agent marker, so the compliant form is the attend event with no ordinal atom at all plus a recorded gap — the same disposal the sequence/ordering adverbs get ("leave them out and record the gap"), since a mis-slotted atom asserts what the sentence does not say.
notes: "As a Keeper" is arguably under-tensed — the appositive rule gives a typing atom the host clause's wrapper, so (Past (Member coraline_ash keeper)) is the closer form — but the bare atom is true of the sentence's content and well-typed, so it is acceptable improvisation, not a defect. Everything else checks out: seal projection, the two in-seal past perfects emitting no Before, the become/Result state shape with its per-member distribution rule, and the reified-plus-flat dual-emit for the time-modified copular.
